entities.summary: Frederik of Baden was a German nobleman who served as Bishop of Utrecht from 1496 until his resignation in 1517. Born into the House of Baden, he was a member of the noble class and played a significant role in the political and religious landscape of the Holy Roman Empire during the Late Middle Ages. His tenure as Bishop of Utrecht was marked by his efforts to strengthen the church's influence in the region and his involvement in the politics of the Habsburg Empire. Despite his efforts, his legacy was largely overshadowed by the tumultuous events of the Protestant Reformation and the subsequent Thirty Years' War. The city of Utrecht, which Frederik of Baden called home, would eventually become a key battleground in the conflict. Frederik of Baden's story serves as a microcosm of the complex web of power and religion that defined the late medieval period. He died on October 4, 1517, at the age of unknown, leaving behind a legacy that continues to be felt in the modern-day city of Utrecht.
